2._section_summary: This abstract reports a single validation study (referred to as 'the present study') of the Persian adaptation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) conducted in Tehran, Iran. The sample comprised 568 men and 525 women drawn from seven universities (total N = 1093); the BAS-2 showed a one-factor solution and satisfactory psychometric properties.

3.evidence_source: The present study aimed to examine the factor structure and psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Iran.
3._section_summary: This introduction describes the development of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its revision (BAS-2), and motivates evaluating the Persian BAS-2. The present study aims to examine the factor structure, convergent validity, and internal consistency of the BAS-2 in Iran and hypothesizes that BAS-2 scores will be negatively correlated with BMI and higher among men than women.

4.evidence_source: A total of 1093 university students (568 men and 525 women) were recruited from seven universities in Tehran, Iran.
4._section_summary: This section reports on a single study (Study X) that recruited N = 1093 university students (568 men, 525 women) from seven universities in Tehran, Iran. Participants were aged 18–50 (M = 25.87, SD = 4.66) and had self-reported BMIs ranging 16.14–36.07 (M = 23.69, SD = 3.48).

5.evidence_source: Data collection took place between December 2014 and June 2015 in seven large universities in Tehran (University of Tehran, Sharif University of Technology, Shahid Beheshti University, Tarbiat Modarres University, Islamic Azad University, Shahed University, and Iran University of Medical Sciences).
5._section_summary: This section describes translation/back-translation of the BAS-2 into Persian and a single data collection conducted between December 2014 and June 2015 at seven universities in Tehran, Iran. Participants were university students who completed a paper-and-pencil survey in classroom settings; the BAS-2 was used (BAS-2), and no sample size, age, BMI, racial composition, or correlations with BMI are reported in this section.

6.evidence_source: The present study aimed to examine the factor structure and psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Iran.
6._section_summary: This Discussion summarizes a single study examining the factor structure and psychometric properties of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university sample, finding a one-factor structure and internal consistency for men and women. It reports small positive associations between BAS-2 and self-esteem/life satisfaction, a negative association between BAS-2 and BMI in women and positive associations in men, small positive associations with age, and small sex differences favoring men; limitations include use of a university sample, self-reported BMI, and absence of ethnicity data.

7._section_summary: This discussion reports validation of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university sample, finding a one-factor structure and good internal consistency. 5.evidence_source: The factor structure of the BAS-2 was examined using a principal-axis exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with quartimax rotation (because of the expectation of a single factor; see Swami & Ng, 2015; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b).
5._section_summary: This section describes the statistical analyses: the factor structure of the BAS-2 was examined via principal-axis exploratory factor analysis with quartimax rotation, using eigenvalues >1, scree plot inspection, and parallel analysis for factor retention. The EFA was conducted separately for women and men; ten independent t-tests compared BAS-2 items by gender and an additional t-test compared total BAS-2 scores, while Pearson correlations were used to examine associations among body appreciation, self-esteem, life satisfaction, BMI, and age.

6._section_summary: This section reports factor-analytic results for the male subsample examining 10 BAS-2 items: KMO = 0.86, Bartlett's test significant, parallel analysis and scree plot supported a single factor explaining 49.9% of variance, and all items loaded adequately. It also reports internal consistency of the BAS-2 in men (Cronbach's α = .89).
